title: Public election, salience and policy evidence for the midterm issue report

scope.purpose: Triangulate opinion, election relevance, policy authority and macro context; not a complete census of all public documents.
scope.date_rule: Include source publications, or explicitly dated source sections, no later than the freeze. No September 8 date-only news item is used. Standing undated rules are separate background.
scope.retrieval_rule: Manual extraction from opened primary-source pages/PDFs using web tools. Sources were read after the freeze but pre-freeze publication/data vintages were selected. This is not a historical page-archive capture.
scope.quote_policy: No long direct quotations; survey questions are paraphrased. Follow source links for exact questionnaires and methods.

schema_notes.date: ISO date of release, official action or explicitly dated document section; null for standing undated background. Consult publication_precision/date_basis.
schema_notes.published_at: Exact ISO timestamp only if verified; null does not mean midnight.
schema_notes.claim: Concise sourced fact or explicitly attributed forecast; not an estimated investment return.
schema_notes.observations: Metric/value/unit/date/population objects; repeated waves have distinct dates/populations.
schema_notes.sample: Latest-wave sample/method information; do not assign it to earlier waves.
schema_notes.question: Paraphrase, not verbatim questionnaire wording.
schema_notes.trend_status: Comparability applies to the indicated question and population, not automatically every observation in a mixed record.
schema_notes.uncertainty: Interpretation, time-vintage and scope restrictions needed for downstream reporting.

analysis_rules: Keep topic attention, prompted concern, open-ended priority, policy preference, voting intention, market-implied prices and enacted policy as separate dimensions.

Only compare the same pollster, question, response options and target population over time; report changes in percentage points and do not infer significance without earlier-wave n/design information.
Registered voters, likely voters, all adults and partisan subgroups must not be pooled as equivalent populations.
Do not extrapolate one state poll to all states, or convert a national generic ballot into a seat-count prediction.
Policy stages are not ordinal enactment probabilities: proposal, passed bill, veto, executive order, rule and implementation can follow different legal paths.
Use these dated primary documents to inspect Kalshi changes; Kalshi mentions/volume measure contract attention or trading, not public salience or directional positioning.
Absence of an issue in this selected evidence packet is missing evidence, not proof the issue lacks importance.
Investment implications in the companion memo are reasoned hypotheses to test against valuation and company exposure, not realized-return findings.
